findings.note: True: AGENTS.md lists an empty log as an emission refusal and verify_chain returns Unverifiable on an empty log (src/decision.rs:178), but docs/adopting.md:105 omits 'empty'; a small doc inconsistency.

run() lets --now override signed_at for v3 (src/baseline.rs:1367), and the Expired branch always says 'the manifest's signed_at is outside the key's validity window' (src/baseline.rs:1087), which is false when --now set the judged time; this is G6's second part.

ADR 0016 says to re-derive the head and compare it exactly, with a mismatch as FAIL; the code (src/baseline.rs:1047) implements that rule, so the finding questions a documented design decision rather than a defect.
tests/baseline.rs:699-700 asserts only a non-empty head and entries >= 1 against the real repo log, so a wrong head or count cannot fail; this is G3.
The --now value goes unvalidated into TrustFile::state (src/baseline.rs:1213 and 466-481), so an empty string or '0' sorts below every revoked_at/valid_until and reads as Trusted; this is G1.

fixture_head() builds its value with decision::head itself (tests/baseline.rs:44-47) and every fixture log has one record, so nothing pins head or entries independently; this is G3's missing independent oracle.
tests/baseline.rs:229 is new and compares canonical_bytes(&forward) with itself, so it cannot fail and does not test the byte stability across runs that its comment claims.
Same point as F03: comparing the whole log's head is what ADR 0016 prescribes ('re-derives the head ... a mismatch is FAIL'), so this is a design question, not a defect in the change.

True: from_json (src/baseline.rs:239-256) checks only that signed_at is present, and state() truncates it, so signed_at '' is judged Trusted; but signed_at sits inside the signed bytes and a signer could backdate a valid timestamp just as easily, so the practical gain is small; this concerns signed_at, not G1's --now.
The canonical-bytes pin fills in head.hash and head.entries from fixture_head(), which calls decision::head (tests/baseline.rs:211), so the pin cannot catch a regression in head(); this is G3.
Same as F09: an unvalidated v3 signed_at reaches state(), where '' sorts low; the parse and emit paths disagree, but the signer controls signed_at regardless, so the impact is limited.

TrustedKey::valid_from is parsed (src/baseline.rs:427) but state() checks only revoked_at and valid_until (466-481); now that the key is judged at a historical signed_at, a time before valid_from reads as Trusted.
True of the shell '>' redirect in docs/adopting.md:96, but req's exit 3 is visible to the person running it, so this is a small doc hardening.

Emission is a refusal rather than a verdict, and AGENTS.md and docs/adopting.md:105 both say emission refuses with exit 3 on a tampered log, so the code (src/baseline.rs:1279-1286) matches the documented contract.
valid_signing_time accepts any day in 1..=31 whatever the month (src/baseline.rs:1426+), so 2026-02-31 is accepted into the signed bytes; this is G6's first part.
